evidence.claim: Cboe: SPX 0DTE market-maker net gamma is small vs S&P futures liquidity
evidence.number: $170mm to $670mm; 0.04% to 0.17% of daily S&P futures liquidity
evidence.quote: "On average, market maker positioning is fairly de minimis, with net gamma exposure ranging from $170mm to $670mm throughout the day. To put that number in context, S&P futures trade around $400bn a day, so we're talking about potential hedging flows that make up between 0.04% to 0.17% of the daily S&P futures liquidity."
evidence.location: point 1 under the 30-min box plot (line 334 of saved md)
evidence.source: Mandy Xu, Cboe, "Volatility Insights: Much Ado About 0DTEs", 2023-09-07/08, https://www.cboe.com/insights/posts/volatility-insights-evaluating-the-market-impact-of-spx-0-dte-options
evidence.grade: exchange-regulator (exchange with commercial interest in 0DTE volume)

evidence.claim: Cboe: net gamma at 3:30 pm and tails
evidence.number: median +$173mm; IQR -$1.1bn to +$2.4bn; whiskers -$5bn to +$7.7bn = 1.3%-1.9% of futures notional
evidence.quote: "The median net gamma at 3:30pm is just +$173mm with the typical range from -$1.1bn to +$2.4bn (25th to 75th percentile readings). Even if we focus on the "whiskers" on the box plot, the range of -$5bn to +$7.7bn represents just 1.3% to 1.9% of the S&P futures daily notional volume."

evidence.claim: Cboe: scope caveat (only SPX 0DTE, not other expiries, ES options or SPY)
evidence.quote: "It's worth noting that this analysis is only for market maker positioning in SPX 0DTE options. Market makers may have offsetting positions in other expiries, or other equivalent products (e.g. E-mini or SPY 0DTE options)."

evidence.claim: Cboe: no rise in 1-min 2-sigma jumps, incl. last hour
evidence.quote: "there has been no uptick in intraday gap moves in the S&P over the past year, either during the trading day or in the last hour going into the close"
